thread:
Amal K.: heads-up — SCIM bulk provisioning started failing after yesterday's KMS key rollover. Several customers have 'dead-letter' entries and new role-mappings aren't applying. audit logs show decrypt errors.
Jordan L.: ugh. can you paste the specific error from the DLQ?
Amal K.: here — snippet from provisioning-worker logs: 
```
2026-03-19T22:11:03Z ERROR provisioning dead_letter enqueue failed key=alias/redwood-2026 KMS_DECRYPT_FAILED: InvalidCiphertextException
resource=user:acct:12345 action=upsert body_ref=msg_98765
```
Nate S.: that alias is the rotated key. did the KMS alias swap complete for the private deployment? sometimes the control plane sees the new alias but workers still have cached DEK.
Amal K.: control-plane shows key=alias/redwood-2026 active. workers on dedicated pool still failing. also seeing 409s when we retry SCIM upserts.
Sara P.: 409 could be because partial RBAC state changed while the retry was in flight. Are there racey role transforms? We had the v2 role-map rollout last week.
Jordan L.: confirm: did the key rotation include re-wrapping existing DEKs? If not, decrypt will fail when the KMS CMK changes.
Amal K.: ops run the rotation with rewrap=true in the script. but the rewrap job logs show timeouts against a handful of DEKs. those entries got moved to DLQ.
infra-bot: FYI — rewrap job completed with 99.87% success. 43 objects failed and moved to dead-letter queue. See https://internal.ops/reports/rewrap-2026-03-19
Nate S.: okay. plan: 1) don't retry bulk upserts until DLQ items are addressed (we risk duplicate partial state), 2) attempt targeted re-decrypt via a small worker with increased KMS timeouts, 3) if decrypt can't be fixed, re-encrypt with new CMK using plaintext fallback but only after approval.
Amal K.: agreed. can security/compliance weigh in on the plaintext re-encrypt fallback? that's a potential sensitive move. @Compliance Bot?
Compliance Bot: quick note — plaintext fallback requires an approved override ticket and must be executed in an air-gapped worker with KMS audit logging enabled and retention bumped to 7 years. Also we need an entry in the incident register mentioning affected orgs.
Jordan L.: ok we need to assemble the incident packet. Also add an evaluation of whether audited SAML assertions or SCIM payloads left logs in ephemeral storage.
Sara P.: i'm worried about RBAC drift: if some SCIM upserts partially applied (user created but roles not set), customers might see permission gaps. We should capture a list of impacted users per org and plan a safe backfill.
Amal K.: I've made a small query to enumerate DLQ keys and affected accounts. putting results in the incident folder — https://internal.sec/incidents/2443216789/artefacts.csv
Nate S.: I'll spin a canary worker in the on-prem tenant and increase KMS retries to 10 with exponential backoff. Command I'm running: 
```sh
./provision-worker --dlq-claim msg_981..999 --kms-tries=10 --kms-timeout-ms=12000 --dry-run=false
```
Amal K.: leave dry-run=false only on the canary; we don't want mass retries yet. Also record all actions in the incident timeline.
Jordan L.: if the canary succeed, we still need a safe retry window and rate-limit for customers to avoid thundering herd. Suggest: 1 req/s per tenant for 24h with a rolling backfill.
Compliance Bot: add checklist: notify affected customers within SLA window, maintain encrypted records of the attempted plaintext rewrap (if used), and preserve original DLQ blobs for forensic review.
infra-bot: deploy-bot rolled out small worker image with extended KMS timeouts to pool=private-rotations at 2026-03-20T00:12Z.
deploy-bot: deploy succeeded on 3/3 nodes in canary pool :tada:
Nate S.: canary did decrypt 12/12 previously-failed items. one item still fails with InvalidCiphertextException referencing key-id mismatch. I'm collecting the item and will attempt a manual decrypt with the previous CMK alias.
Amal K.: excellent. Nate, coordinate with infra to get temporary read access to prior CMK alias and log the action. Jordan, can you draft the customer message template for possible permission gaps? keep it conservative.
Jordan L.: drafting now. key points: what happened, who is affected, mitigation steps, CI of audit logs available on request. Will ping for review in ~20m.
Sara P.: after remediation, we need a validation job: re-run a small subset of SCIM updates and verify role parity vs snapshot taken at 2026-03-19T21:50Z. I'll own the validation and will add a postmortem action item to fix retry semantics.
Amal K.: thanks all. tagging @oncall for visibility. we'll keep incident open until DLQ empty and RBAC parity verified.
Nate S.: manual decrypt succeeded for the one remaining item after we fetched the old key alias from KMS archive. scheduling backfill now, running at 0.5qps to minimize disruption.
Compliance Bot: note recorded: incident_id=IR-2026-0319-01, classification=high-sensitivity, customers_notified=false (pending draft).
Amal K.: closing note: no evidence of exfiltration, issue was key-rotation rewrap timeout causing DLQ. action items created: rewrap job retries, DLQ watcher alert, operator runbook update, customer comms. I'll file the postmortem tomorrow. :white_check_mark:
